Three ways to travel
What I plan

So — what kind of trip are you after?

I plan the three things I'm best at, and I've experienced them first hand.

Cruises

Ocean, river, and expedition. The difference between a good cruise and a disappointing one is almost always the ship and the cabin — not the itinerary.

All-Inclusive Resorts

One price, nothing to decide once you land. I match the resort to the trip — adults-only, swim-up, family-friendly — and get the perks attached before you arrive.

Why use an advisor at all

Three things a booking site can't do

Perks you can't add yourself

Through Signature Travel Network I can attach resort credits, room upgrades where they're available, and onboard credit on many sailings. All on the same published rate you'd pay booking direct.

A person when it goes wrong

Flight cancelled, transfer never showed, wrong room at check-in. You call me instead of waiting in line or sitting on hold with an offshore call center.

No cost, in most cases

On the great majority of cruise, resort, and tour bookings I'm paid a commission by the supplier after you travel. If a trip ever needs a planning fee, you'll know the number before you commit.

How it works

What happens once you get in touch?

  1. Consultation

    A free call about where you want to go, who's coming, and how you like to travel. No obligation and no script.

  2. Proposal

    Two or three real options with what each one includes, what it costs, and why I picked it. Not forty tabs of search results.

  3. Booking

    I handle the reservation, the deposits, the payment schedule, and the perks. You get a full itinerary before you leave.

  4. Support

    You travel with my number in your phone. Anything goes sideways, that's my problem to solve, not yours.

Fees, process, and the questions everyone asks

Meet your advisor

Strategy by trade, wanderer by heart

I came to travel from project management. Less romantic than most advisors' origin stories — far more useful. This job is mostly logistics, and logistics is what I'm good at.

My husband Chad and I live full-time in our RV, so travel isn't a thing I read about in a supplier newsletter. I've been on the ships. I've walked the resorts. When I tell you a cabin category is worth the upgrade, it's because I've slept in it.
